confirmed.what_breaks: Planted defect src/domain/customers.js:55 'orderCount > 0' -> 'orderCount > 1' survived. With it, a customer with exactly one order can be deleted, and that order is left with no customer. No test deletes a customer who has exactly one order.
confirmed.evidence: mutate.mjs: survived src/domain/customers.js:55 "0" -> "1". The R-05 refusal test uses 2 orders for c1 (lines 92-96), and 2 > 1 still refuses. The R-05 delete test uses 0 orders.

confirmed.what_breaks: Planted defect src/domain/orders.js:30 'ok: false' -> 'ok: true' survived. An unknown order would return ok:true with no state. app.js commit() would then call store.save(undefined), and the stored data would be overwritten.
confirmed.evidence: mutate.mjs: survived src/domain/orders.js:30 "false" -> "true". Test line 79 checks only `.errors.order` and never checks `ok === false`. app.js lines 54-55 save result.state whenever result.ok is true.

confirmed.what_breaks: Planted defect src/domain/orders.js:32 (bad date) 'ok: false' -> 'ok: true' survived. The same path as VER-3 would save undefined over the stored data when the user enters an invalid date.
confirmed.evidence: mutate.mjs: survived src/domain/orders.js:32 "false" -> "true". Test line 78 checks only `.errors.date`.

confirmed.what_breaks: Planted defect src/storage/store.js:61 'loaded = true' -> 'loaded = false' survived. After a reload of existing data, every save would be refused, so the app could no longer persist changes. No test saves after loading data that already exists.
confirmed.evidence: mutate.mjs: survived src/storage/store.js:61 "true" -> "false". In the R-17 round-trip test, the second store only calls load() and never calls save().

confirmed.what_breaks: Planted defect src/domain/orders.js:38 '===' -> '!==' survived. Deleting the only order would be refused, and an unknown id on a non-empty list would be accepted. The unknown-order test uses an empty orders list.
confirmed.evidence: mutate.mjs: survived src/domain/orders.js:38 "===" -> "!==". Test line 92 is deleteOrder(stateWith([]), 'nope'), and some() on [] is false either way. The R-09 delete test has 2 orders.

confirmed.what_breaks: Planted defect src/domain/lines.js:47 '===' -> '!==' survived. Editing the only line of an order would be refused, and editing an unknown line on a non-empty order would report success. The unknown-line test uses an order with no lines.
confirmed.evidence: mutate.mjs: survived src/domain/lines.js:47 "===" -> "!==". Test line 89 is updateLine(stateWith(), ...) with lines []. The R-13 edit test has 3 lines.

confirmed.what_breaks: When stored data cannot be loaded, ctx.state falls back to a copy of the empty state kept in the UI. Next to the error banner, the lists then say 'No customers yet. Use "Add customer"...', although the data exists and every control is disabled.
confirmed.evidence: app.js line 14 defines emptyState and line 19 returns it when store.current() is null, which is the case after a failed load (store.js lines 57-58 leave state null). customers-view.js buildResults shows the 'No customers yet' text when customers.length === 0. disableForms (app.js line 48) disables the Add button.

confirmed.what_breaks: The load check tests types only. Hand-edited data loads as valid in four cases: nextOrderNumber at or below an existing order number (the next order then reuses a number, against A-04), an order whose customerId points to no customer, duplicate ids, and negative amounts (formatEuros(-5) gives '€-1.-5'). The app's own UI cannot produce any of these states.
confirmed.evidence: hasValidShape (lines 25-29) calls only isObject, Number.isInteger and typeof string checks. The object {version:1,nextOrderNumber:1,orders:[{number:1,...,lines:[{quantity:-3,unitPriceCents:-5}]}]} passes every check. addOrder (orders.js line 19) assigns state.nextOrderNumber, which is 1 again. formatEuros: Math.floor(-0.05) is -1 and String(-5 % 100).padStart(2,'0') is '-5'. Traced by reading the code: node one-liners are refused by the guard in this session.

confirmed.what_breaks: The email rule is stricter than R-02. A domain part that starts or ends with a dot ('a@b.com.', 'a@.com') has one @, text on both sides and a dot after the @, yet it is refused. PLAN S2 Risks says 'nothing stricter'. tests/customers.test.js line 46 locks in the refusal of 'a@.'.
confirmed.evidence: isValidEmail returns false when domain.startsWith('.') or domain.endsWith('.'). For 'a@b.com.', the domain 'b.com.' ends with '.', so validateCustomer sets errors.email. Severity is advisory: no data is lost, and the refused inputs are not deliverable addresses.

confirmed.what_breaks: The order filter keeps view.customerId after that customer is deleted. Back on the Orders tab, the select has no matching option, but the filter still applies, so 'No orders match your filter.' shows while orders exist.
confirmed.evidence: view.customerId is module state (line 8) and is never reset. R-05 lets a customer be deleted only when they have no orders, so filterOrders with that customerId returns []. buildResults line 73 then shows the no-match text. The user can recover by picking 'All customers'.

confirmed.what_breaks: The list shows order numbers as '#12' (orders-view.js line 81), but typing '#12' in the filter finds nothing, because the needle is compared with String(o.number).
confirmed.evidence: For needle '#12', '12'.includes('#12') is false, and no customer name contains '#', so the result is [].

confirmed.what_breaks: PLAN S7 step 4 ('opening an order from the customer view') is not done. The customer's order rows are plain text, and app.js wires only the tab switching.
confirmed.evidence: customers-view.js line 102 is el('td', `#${order.number}`) with no button. app.js lines 65-71 hold only switchTab. customers-view.js is not on the S7 Files line (PLAN line 164), so the plan made the step impossible inside S7. R-04 itself (fields, orders, totals) is met.

confirmed.what_breaks: The DOM helpers el and button exist twice. lines-view.js exports them for orders-view.js, and customers-view.js keeps its own copy.
confirmed.evidence: lines-view.js lines 7-18 export el and button, orders-view.js line 6 imports them, and customers-view.js lines 9-20 repeat them. The S6 and S7 Files lines name no shared UI module.

confirmed.what_breaks: CI checks out ioanbitza/sdlc-kit without a ref or sha and runs its gate.mjs. A change upstream changes what CI enforces, with no change in this repository.
confirmed.evidence: gate.yml: the second actions/checkout step has repository and path but no 'ref:', followed by 'node .sdlc-kit/tools/gate.mjs --strict'. ADR-002 does not say whether the gate version is pinned.

watchList.what_breaks: window.localStorage is read at module top level with no try. In a browser that blocks site data, the getter throws a SecurityError, the module stops, and no banner is shown.
watchList.evidence: Line 5: const store = createStore(window.localStorage); store.load guards only getItem.
watchList.why_unproven: Needs a browser with site data blocked; no browser was available in this session.
watchList.how_to_settle: In Chrome, block all site data for localhost, reload http://localhost:8000, and check whether the banner shows an error or the page is blank.

watchList.what_breaks: crypto.randomUUID exists only in secure contexts. Served over plain http on a LAN IP, newId throws inside the submit handlers, and Add customer, New order and Add line fail without a message on the page.
watchList.evidence: newId is called unguarded at customers-view.js:158, orders-view.js:123 and lines-view.js:105. AGENTS.md documents localhost, which is a secure context.
watchList.why_unproven: Needs a browser on a non-localhost http origin; the documented run uses localhost, where this does not happen.
watchList.how_to_settle: Serve with python3 -m http.server 8000, open http://<LAN-IP>:8000, add a customer and watch the console and the page.

watchList.what_breaks: The empty state 'This customer has no orders yet.' offers no next action, such as creating an order for this customer.
watchList.evidence: The text is el('p', 'This customer has no orders yet.'). R-20 names 'no orders' but does not say whether a customer's own order list is one of its states.
watchList.why_unproven: R-20 can be read either way. The code behaviour is clear, but whether it breaks the requirement is not.
watchList.how_to_settle: The human says whether R-20 covers the customer view's order list; if it does, add a 'New order for this customer' action (this needs customers-view.js in a slice).

watchList.what_breaks: centsToInput formats cents as euro text in the UI, repeating the arithmetic of formatEuros from money.js.
watchList.evidence: lines-view.js line 20-21. PLAN line 'Text becomes cents only in src/domain/money.js' covers text to cents, not cents to text.
watchList.why_unproven: Whether cents-to-input-text is a business rule under AGENTS.md is a judgement no rule settles.
watchList.how_to_settle: The human decides; if yes, move it to money.js with a test such as 'R-13 1250 cents edits as "12.50"'.

watchList.what_breaks: Commit b00627a ticks every manual check at once under 'Manual checks'. Nothing in the repository shows which checks a human actually ran.
watchList.evidence: git log shows b00627a by Bita Ioan with every '- [ ]' changed to '- [x]'. ADR-002 says the human ticks only the checks they ran. Rule 8 applies to slice commits, and this is not a slice commit.
watchList.why_unproven: Authorship cannot show whether the checks were performed.
watchList.how_to_settle: The human confirms in their own terminal that they ran each ticked check, or unticks the ones not run.

decisions.note: Fix the six blocking ones and the three defects a user can see: the wrong empty message on a load error, the stale customer filter, and the #12 search. The stricter email rule is what I want, hand-edited data is out of scope for this build, the clickable orders in the customer view and the shared DOM helpers go to a later slice, and the CI pin is a repo chore I will do myself.
